scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A colour printer can copy almost anything. So why is it so hard to copy a currency note?

scenes.name: paper
scenes.text: Notes are printed on special cotton based paper, not wood pulp, so they feel crisp and different.

scenes.name: watermark
scenes.text: Hold a note up to light and you see a watermark. It's made inside the paper, not printed on top.

scenes.name: thread
scenes.text: A security thread is woven in, and on many notes its colour shifts when you tilt it.

scenes.name: intaglio
scenes.text: Raised intaglio printing makes parts of the note feel bumpy, which also helps visually impaired people.

scenes.name: micro
scenes.text: Tiny micro letters are printed so small, that most home printers blur them.

scenes.name: uv
scenes.text: Some inks glow under UV light, and banks use machines to check features you can't see.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Paper, watermark, thread, raised print. Hard to copy, easy to check. Follow for more on how things really work.
